quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Get out and wave down the next vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency lights, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency lights, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency lights to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if possible. Interstate traffic moves very fast, making it dangerous to stand or walk along the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle breaks down?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic as soon as possible. Turn on your emergency lights so other drivers can see you have a problem.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Do not wait until your car is moving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure any loose items before you start driving.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Any child age 12 or under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibration and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic behind and to the side of your vehicle before you change lanes. Make sure no vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: You must always obey a police officer's directions, even if they contradict traffic signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to look over one shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in two directions.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that affects your driving ability?

options.text: No, under no circumstances.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if it is prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while using any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription and over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Why should motor vehicle drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may come onto the road suddenly from the sidewalk.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car ahead very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Which of these actions is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or anywhere you cannot see far ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, no passing zones, or where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane. Do not pass if the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones where passing is unsafe.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as on a dry road.
Greater than on a dry road.
Less than on a dry road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greater than on a dry road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on a slippery road. Increase your following distance when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes errors with speed and distance, increases crash risk, and slows your decision-making. When tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash, which can injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Only the windshield.
All windows.
Only the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: Which of these is not a safe practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before moving your vehicle left or right. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. Never back up or make a U-turn on the interstate. If you miss your exit, drive to the next exit.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic signal that is not working?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection looks clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Always come to a complete stop unless a police officer tells you otherwise. Look and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
It distracts other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. Even experienced drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone on the road.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: Still wear your seat belt.
You do not need to wear a seat belt.
Wear your seat belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are safety devices that help protect you in a crash. For the best protection, always use your seat belt along with airbags.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Wait for your body to process it.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process it.
questions.explanation: Nothing speeds up how your body removes alcohol — not cold showers, coffee, or exercise. The only way to lower your blood alcohol level is to wait.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the road while driving?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and be careful.
Quickly move to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move into traffic. Animals often travel in groups, so there may be more animals you cannot see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign tells you there is a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: What happens if you drive slower than traffic?

options.text: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
You improve traffic flow.
You show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can block traffic flow and result in a ticket. Drive at the same speed as traffic unless traffic exceeds the speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass first. You can turn when the intersection is clear and the traffic signal allows it.

questions.question: Where should you look before entering an intersection?

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. This helps you see vehicles from both directions. Vehicles from the left will be closer, so check that direction twice.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Try to fight the drowsiness.
Stop and rest.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills are not a safe replacement for real rest.

questions.question: If your seat belt has a lap and shoulder belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.
